title: The importance of cardio for bodybuilding & overall health
summary: NH separates cardio for health from cardio for performance and argues a bodybuilder needs enough cardiovascular endurance never to be limited by it in a set. He does no separate cardio himself, ranks options (fartlek outside on top, treadmill at the bottom), and builds conditioning through giant sets and heavy high-rep compounds.
claims: He does not do cardio in the conventional way
Cardio means either straining the cardiovascular system or the activities people do for that; if you lift you already do some
Cardio should be specific to your goal: athletes should mimic how their sport moves the body
Cardio for health and cardio for performance are separate; cardiovascular stamina can be good while cardiovascular health is poor, which also depends on diet and lifestyle
For a bodybuilder the point of cardio is endurance so high you are never limited by it; stopping a squat set out of breath means your heart and lungs limited the set
Cardiovascular recovery between sessions is fast compared to muscle rebuilding; it matters mainly within the workout
Calorie-burning cardio both uses energy and builds the cardiovascular system whether you want it or not
With his low appetite, burning extra calories would be counterproductive, so he never does cardio to burn calories
The classic hour of lifting plus 30 minutes of treadmill is not bad but can waste time and lack specificity
If you do separate gym cardio, prefer the stepper (builds calves and posterior chain) or jump rope over the treadmill; incline treadmill if you must
Jogging is already not great for cardio and the treadmill is a weaker version of running
Best cardio is outdoors; never run on pavement or stone because it damages the knees; run on dirt, grass or sand
Fartlek (5-10 second sprints alternated with about a minute of jogging until exhausted) is top tier: time efficient and mimics how heavy lifting taxes the heart
He shovels snow in winter and does fast mountain hikes in summer as a test that his endurance is still there, not to build it
He trained for football and basketball, with about 80% of training being running, hill sprints and beach fartlek, and kept that endurance
Health and longevity are primordial; he wants to be mobile and strong at 70-80
He builds his cardiovascular system with giant sets of movements done with no breaks, moving cardio inside training and saving time
Supersetting stiff-legged deadlifts with rows is too demanding on the lower back and cardio for 99% of people
He does not recommend that people do cardio only through weight training
Heavy squats for high reps or heavy deadlifts for moderately high reps are compressed high-intensity cardio
Specificity matters: training high-rep squats carries over to breathing during heavy squats better than sprints do, and vice versa for runners
Do a cardio activity you like on the side, such as swimming or hiking
Do not be the guy who lifts heavy but gets winded on stairs; that also correlates with body fat
exercises: 5-10s sprint, ~1 min jog, outdoors on soft ground
his cardio giant set; too demanding for most
